correctness.rationale: Multiplication of the four k[t]-module blocks gives a²+t^(n−2)bc=0 in R_n, b(a+d)=c(a+d)=0 in R_2, and d²=0 in R_2 because n≥4. In particular d_0=0; the lowest nonzero coefficient of a² cannot be cancelled below t^(n−2), even in characteristic two. For n=2h this leaves the equations x²+BC=2xy+BV+CU=δB=δC=0 and h−1 free coefficients, with δ=d_1+x when n=4 and δ=d_1 otherwise. The component B=C=x=0 is affine; the branch δ=0 is a dimension-four complete intersection whose B≠0 open is irreducible (solve for C,V) and whose B=0 complement has dimension at most three (x=0, CU=0). For n=2h+1 one has BC=0, x²+BV+CU=0 and δB=δC=0, with h free coefficients; the three branches are the affine B=C=x=0 branch and the two geometrically irreducible quadratic cones with a free coordinate. The quadratic cone equations are primitive linear polynomials in one of B,C,U,V over the polynomial ring in the remaining variables, so this holds in characteristic two. The stated intersections follow as reduced varieties; this makes no scheme-theoretic assertion about the sum of the odd cone ideals. Partitioning field points by B=C=0 versus its complement gives q^(h−1)[q^4+(q²−1)q²] or q^h[q³+2(q−1)q²] as stated. A separate binary commutator-kernel calculation (python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py) gave 56,64,112,128 for n=4,5,6,7, respectively. The proof, not that finite check or the reported original runs, supplies every-field and every-q validity.
